title: Latency-aware region steering and tiered spillover policy for dedicated→hosted routing
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines an operational policy and implementation plan for steering requests by region and tier, with deterministic and probabilistic spillover rules from Dedicated capacity to Hosted when capacity or regional constraints are hit. Focus is on latency-aware region selection, per-tenant SLO preservation, model-variant compatibility scoring, and safeguards to avoid cascading failures and cost spikes.

Problem statement:
Customers on Dedicated pools sometimes experience transient capacity shortages (node preemption, autoscaler lag, runtime throttles). Current default spillover to Hosted is coarse-grained and can generate high-latency cross-region routing and unexpected token billing. We need a predictable, observable policy that:
- prefers same-region fallbacks when they meet latency SLOs,
- respects customer tier (enterprise vs free) and billing constraints,
- selects fallback model variants (quantized, smaller, or alternative architecture) using a compatibility+quality penalty score,
- enforces safety throttles to prevent large-scale spillover cascades.

Goals and non-goals:
Goals:
- Provide deterministic steering decisions that minimize median latency and tail latency regressions for affected tenants.
- Bound cost exposure during spillover (max fallback qps and token rate per tenant).
- Make routing decisions auditable and configurable per-tenant with sane defaults.
Non-goals:
- Full rewrite of autoscaler. This ticket augments routing/orchestration only.

Proposed policy components:
1) Region selection algorithm (latency-aware):
- Maintain per-region P95 and P99 synthetic latency estimates for each model family.
- For a Dedicated→Hosted spillover, compute candidate regions that satisfy estimated P95 < tenant.SLO_latency_threshold * 1.15 (configurable margin).
- Prioritize same-region candidates; if none meet SLO, expand to neighboring regions sorted by estimated latency.
- If no region meets P95 margin, fall back to local degraded-mode (serve smaller model variant or gated deny with informative error).

2) Tier routing policy (tenant priority & billing constraints):
- Tenants have tier metadata: enterprise, standard, trial. Policy table: { enterprise: prefer same-region hosted, allow cross-region at reduced penalty; standard: allow cross-region if latency delta < 200ms; trial: best-effort only }.
- Allow per-tenant overrides via Dedicated config: 'spillover_policy' with values {always_prefer_hosted_same_region, disallow_cross_region, cost_capped}.

3) Model-variant fallback selection (compatibility scoring):
- Each model in catalog publishes variant descriptors (size, quant, expected quality score delta, compatible tokenizers).
- Compute a variant_score = quality_penalty * 100 + token_cost_multiplier * 10 + region_penalty (lower is better).
- Only consider variants where compatibility flags match (e.g., forcing same tokenizer for safety of structured output).

4) Safety throttles and admission controls:
- Global spillover circuit breaker: if Hosted_inbound_spill_rate > 15% of hosted capacity sustained over 30s, stop non-enterprise spillovers and trigger operator alert.
- Per-tenant cap: max_spill_qps and max_spill_tokens configurable; exceeding these will queue/deny until Dedicated recovers.
- Priority decay window: After a spillover, tenant priority decays linearly over 10 minutes to avoid repeated immediate spillovers.

5) Observability and audit trail:
- Emit structured events for each routing decision: {tenant, source_pool, decision, latency_estimates, chosen_region, chosen_variant, reason_code}.
- Surface a Spillover dashboard in Console with per-tenant timelines, cost delta estimate, and SLO impact.

Acceptance criteria:
- Implementation routes spillover requests using the latency-aware algorithm in a deterministic dry-run mode (no actual reroute) with logs matching expected decisions for provided test vectors.
- Canary rollout to 5% of tenants in prod Hosted where decisions switch from old heuristic to new policy; metrics show no >5% median latency regression and billed token delta <= 10% for canary group over 24h.
- Circuit breaker triggers in simulated overload tests and prevents non-enterprise spillovers.

Design doc and artifacts:
- Confluence spec (draft): https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/RVR/Latency-aware+Spillover+Policy
- Decision log and math: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/RVR/Spillover+Scoring+Matrix
- Reference PR (routing changes): https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/6543
- Telemetry dashboards prototype: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/Spillover/hosted-spillover-dashboard

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (QA): unit tests + local simulation harness (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (Dry-run): route decisions logged but not enforced for subset of tenants (1 week).
- Phase 2 (Canary): 5% enforcement, 24–72h observation, rollback gate (SLO regressions, cost spike).
- Phase 3 (Gradual rollout): 25% → 50% → 100% with monitoring alerts and runbook for manual rollback.

Testing and validation:
- Create synthetic trace generator to simulate Dedicated saturation patterns and verify chosen fallback regions and variants.
- Chaos test: kill 1 regional Dedicated pool and validate safe throttles prevent spillover storms.
- Billing test: synthetic tenants with cap policies to assert cost_capped behaves correctly.

Open questions / Risks:
- How to maintain accurate per-region latency estimates when models are new or under-sampled? Mitigation: fall back to cross-region historical baselines and mark decisions as lower-confidence.
- Regulatory constraints: some tenants must never cross region. Need server-side enforcement and API to set per-tenant region lock.
- Potential billing surprise for tenants when fallback model incurs higher token usage. Mitigation: include pre-spillover cost estimation in audit event and tenant-level notification hooks.

Next steps / action items:
- Implement scoring library and add synthetic latency store (ENG: Leon/Kayla)
- Add routing policy config API and per-tenant overrides (ENG: Leonard)
- Wire telemetry events and dashboard (ENG: Pilar)
- Create QA harness + canary gating in Console (PM: Rafael)

Estimated work breakdown (high-level):
- Scoring & decision engine: 3 pts
- Policy config API + per-tenant flags: 2 pts
- Telemetry & dashboards: 2 pts
- Integration + canary infra: 1 pt
